title: 404 page
about: The page shown when an address does not exist; its job is to get the visitor back on track.

items.t: Plain words: "We cannot find that page", without the word "404" as the headline
A short reason: the address may be mistyped, or the page moved
No blame on the visitor
Calm humour only if it does not hide the message
A search box
Links to the home page and the most used pages
A contact link to report a broken link
The site's normal header and footer so navigation still works
Returns the status 404 (or 410 for gone forever), not 200
Moved pages redirect (301) to their new home instead of showing a 404
Broken links found in logs and fixed
The page title says "Page not found" with the site name
One main heading, contrast and phone width meet WCAG
Images or illustrations have alt text or are hidden if decorative

title: About page
about: Tells visitors who the company is, why it exists and why they can trust it.

items.t: One sentence on what the company does and for whom, at the top
The story: when and why it started, in a few short paragraphs
Mission or purpose in plain words, not slogans
What makes the company different, with facts
Founders and leaders with real photos, names and roles
Team size or a link to the Team page
Photos of real people and places, not stock images
Numbers that matter: customers, years, countries, with the date they were true
Customer logos or quotes used with permission
Awards, press mentions and partners, linked to the source
Investors or ownership, if relevant to trust
Physical address and registered company name
A way to get in touch from the page
Links to Careers, Press and Contact
Short paragraphs, headings and lists for scanning
Headings that say what each part is about
Images have alt text that describes them; decorative ones are hidden from screen readers
Text contrast meets 4.5 to 1
Organization structured data (name, logo, address, links)
Page title that names the company

title: Affiliate page
about: Invites people to promote the product for a commission and explains how the programme works.

items.t: Commission stated plainly: percent or amount, one-off or recurring, for how long
Cookie window (how long after a click a sale still counts)
When and how payouts happen, the minimum payout and the currencies
A worked example: "Refer 10 customers on the Pro plan, earn X a month"
Who can join, and who cannot (for example, no paid search on the brand name)
A short application form; tell people how long approval takes
A sign-in link for existing affiliates
Terms of the programme linked before applying
Affiliates must say clearly that they earn a commission
No false claims, fake reviews or spam to promote the product
Brand guidelines and approved logos to download
Links, banners and text ready to copy
A dashboard showing clicks, sign-ups, sales and money owed
A contact for affiliate questions
Quotes or numbers from current affiliates (real, with permission)
FAQ on tax forms, payment methods and returns that cancel commission
Form fields with visible labels and clear errors
Headings and contrast meet WCAG

title: Billing page (website)
about: The public page that explains how billing works: payment methods, invoices, taxes, refunds and cancelling.

items.t: Payment methods accepted, with logos and words (cards, Apple Pay, mada, bank transfer, invoice)
Currencies offered and which one the customer will be charged in
When the charge happens: at sign-up, at trial end, monthly or yearly on the same date
Taxes (VAT) explained: whether prices include tax and how tax IDs are added
Auto-renewal stated plainly, with the price after any discount ends
What happens on upgrade (charged the difference now) and downgrade (from next period)
Reminder email before a yearly renewal or trial end
How to cancel, in as few steps as it took to sign up
Refund policy in plain words, including the EU 14-day right to withdraw where it applies
How long a refund takes to arrive
Where to find invoices, and that they can be downloaded as PDF
How to add a company name, address and tax ID to invoices
Invoices that meet the local e-invoice rules (for Saudi Arabia, ZATCA)
What happens if a payment fails: retries, grace period, when access stops
Card security: card details handled by a PCI-certified payment provider
A contact for billing questions
FAQ for common questions
Headings, contrast and plain words meet WCAG

title: Blog (list page)
about: The blog's front page that lists articles and helps readers find one to read.

items.t: Newest posts first, with a featured post at the top if useful
Each card: title, short summary, date, author, reading time and image
The whole card opens the post, with one link inside (not many nested links)
Categories or topics to filter
Search over posts
Pagination with page numbers, or Load more that keeps position on Back
Email sign-up with what and how often
RSS feed linked
Cards in a grid that becomes one column on phones
Images have space reserved so the page does not jump
Images lazy-loaded below the fold
Dates in a clear format with the year
One main heading; card titles as headings
Card images decorative (empty alt) when the title already says it
Contrast meets WCAG, including over images
A unique title and description for the list and each category
Breadcrumbs on category pages

title: Blog post
about: A single article page, built for reading, sharing and finding the next article.

items.t: Title as the only top-level heading
Author name with photo and a link to their page
Date published and date updated
Reading time
A summary or key points for scanners
Body text at least 16 pixels, line height about 1.5
Lines of about 50 to 75 characters
Headings every few paragraphs, in order
Short paragraphs, lists and bold key words
A contents list for long posts, with jump links
Links say where they go
Images with alt text and captions; charts also described in words
Code blocks scroll on their own on phones, never the whole page
Text resizes to 200% without breaking
Dark mode respected if the site has one
Share buttons that are links, not heavy trackers
Related posts at the end
A sign-up for new posts, with consent rules
Category and tags linking to more
Comments, if any, moderated
Article structured data: headline, author, dates, image
A unique title and description
Breadcrumbs for deep sites
Images sized and lazy-loaded; the page does not jump
Sponsored or affiliate links disclosed

title: Careers page
about: Shows open jobs and what it is like to work at the company, and takes applications.

items.t: Open jobs listed with title, team, place (or remote) and type (full time, contract)
Filters by team, place and type when there are many
Each job has its own page and address that can be shared
Closed jobs removed promptly
What the job is, what the person will do in the first months, and must-have versus nice-to-have skills
Pay range where the law asks for it (many US states, EU from 2026)
Benefits, working hours and leave
Hiring steps and how long they take
Job structured data so the post appears in job search
A short form; upload a CV instead of retyping it
No account needed to apply
File upload accepts common types with size limits stated
Labels, errors and autofill work
What happens to the applicant's data and for how long it is kept
Confirmation on screen and by email
Real photos and words from staff, with permission
Values, diversity and accessibility commitments, with facts
Adjustments offered for applicants with disabilities
Works at phone width
Headings and contrast meet WCAG

title: Cart page
about: Shows what the shopper is about to buy and the full cost, and moves them to checkout.

items.t: Each item: photo, name, chosen options (size, colour), unit price and quantity
Change quantity with a field plus minus and plus buttons
Remove an item, with Undo instead of a confirmation box
A link back to each product
Stock warnings that are true ("Only 2 left" only if real)
Save for later or move to wishlist
Subtotal, shipping, tax and discounts each on their own line
Shipping cost or an estimate shown before checkout; hidden costs are the top reason people leave
No surprise fees added later; all mandatory fees in the first price shown
Total in the shopper's currency, stating whether tax is included
Delivery date estimate, not only a speed
Promo code field present but low-key (a link that opens it)
One clear Checkout button, at the top and bottom on long carts
Guest checkout offered; forcing an account makes people leave
Express pay buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay) for speed
Continue shopping link
Trust signals near the button: returns policy, secure payment
An empty cart that suggests where to go next
Cart kept across visits and devices for signed-in shoppers
Changes to totals announced to screen readers
Quantity buttons have names ("Increase quantity of Blue mug")
Touch targets at least 24 pixels, 44 recommended
Works at phone width with no sideways scroll

title: Changelog
about: The public list of what changed in each release.

items.t: Newest first, with date and version
Grouped by Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Security
Written for users: what they can do now, not code names
Screenshots or short clips for visible changes
Linked from the product and the footer
Each entry has its own address to share
RSS or email for people who want updates
Breaking changes and removals called out clearly
Security fixes listed
Headings per release and readable images

title: Coming Soon page
about: A holding page before a launch that says what is coming and collects interest.

items.t: What is coming and who it is for, in one line
A rough launch date, or "early 2027", only if the team will keep it
One clear action: leave an email to be told at launch
What the person will get by signing up (early access, a discount)
Company name and a way to contact
One field: email, with a visible label and the right input type
Say exactly what emails will be sent and how often
Consent box unticked by default where the law needs consent for marketing
A link to the privacy policy beside the form
Confirmation on screen and by email; double opt-in where required
Errors shown in words next to the field
A countdown that is real and never resets
Countdown numbers not read aloud every second by screen readers
Returns a normal page (status 200), with a real title and description
If the main site is down for a short while, use a maintenance page instead (status 503)
Contrast and text size meet WCAG
Any background video or animation can be paused and respects reduced motion
Works at phone width with no sideways scroll

title: Compare page
about: Compares the product with a competitor or an alternative, to help a visitor choose.

items.t: Every claim about a competitor is true, current and can be proven
Use the competitor's name only to identify them; no logo that suggests they endorse you
Date of the comparison shown, with the plan or version compared
Prices compared like for like (same plan level, same billing period, taxes stated)
A link to the competitor's own pricing or docs so visitors can check
A short summary at the top: who should pick which
A side-by-side table with the same rows for each product
Rows grouped by topic, with the most important first
Ticks and crosses also carry words or a screen-reader label, not only icons or colour
The header row and first column stay visible while scrolling a long table
Table built with real table headers so screen readers read each cell with its row and column
Where the competitor is better, say so; it builds trust
Quotes from customers who switched, with permission
Help to switch: import tools, migration guide, contact
One main action at the end (start free, talk to sales)
The table stays readable on phones: two products side by side, or stacked cards

title: Contact Us page
about: Lets visitors reach the right person by the way that suits them.

items.t: Several ways: form, email, phone, chat, address, each with when it is answered
Phone numbers as tap-to-call links on phones
Opening hours with the time zone
Expected reply time for each way
Routes for common needs: sales, support, press, billing
Links to self-help (help centre, status page) offered, never forced first
Physical address with a map link
Only the fields needed: name, email, topic, message
Topic as a short list so it reaches the right team
Labels above fields; autofill for name and email
Errors shown next to the field and in a summary at the top
File attachment optional, with types and size limit stated
A robot check only if spam is a real problem, and an accessible one
What happens to the message data, with a privacy link
A confirmation screen with a reference number and what happens next
A copy sent by email
The message is kept if sending fails, so it is not lost
Contact link in the same place on every page
Contrast, target size and phone width meet WCAG

title: Cookie consent
about: Asking before using cookies and trackers that are not strictly needed.

items.t: Consent before any non-essential cookie or tracker is set
Strictly necessary cookies need no consent
Accept and Reject equally easy, on the first layer
No ticked boxes in advance
Plain words on what each kind does, with a link to details
Does not block the page more than needed
Choice by purpose (analytics, marketing)
Changing your mind is as easy as giving consent, from every page
The choice remembered and not asked again on every visit
Consent recorded with time and version
The banner reachable by keyboard and read by screen readers
Focus not trapped and content not hidden behind it

title: Documentation site
about: The help and how-to pages for a product, organised so people find answers.

items.t: Tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanations kept apart
A getting-started page that reaches a first success fast
Left navigation tree and "on this page" headings
Search across all pages with good results for common words
Clear page titles and addresses
Steps numbered, with screenshots that match the current product
Copy buttons on code and commands
Last updated date
"Was this helpful?" on each page
A link to support when the page did not help
Headings, keyboard use, contrast and readable code blocks

title: Event page
about: A page for one event (talk, conference, webinar, launch) that tells people what, when and where, and gets them registered.

items.t: Event name and one line on why to attend
Date and start and end time with the time zone written out
Times shown in the visitor's own time zone for online events, with the original beside it
Place: venue name and full address for in person, "Online" with the platform for virtual
One clear Register or Get tickets button, repeated at the end
Price, or "Free", visible before the button is pressed
Seats left or "Sold out" shown honestly; never fake scarcity
Agenda with times for each part
Speakers with photo, name, role and a short bio
Who it is for and what they will take away
Language of the event
Accessibility at the venue: step-free entry, captions, sign language, quiet room
Directions, map, parking and public transport
What to bring and dress code if any
Refund and transfer policy for tickets
A short form: only the fields needed to attend
Confirmation screen and email with the date, place and a calendar file
Add to calendar for Google, Apple and Outlook
A way to cancel a registration
Reminder email before the event, with the join link for online events
The page changes once the event has passed: "This event has ended" with the recording or slides
No Register button on a past event
Event structured data (name, start date, location, offers, status) so search shows it
Event status marked if cancelled, postponed or moved online
A share image and title for social links
Captions and transcripts for any video
Colour contrast and readable text sizes
Page title includes the event name and date

title: FAQ page
about: Answers the questions people really ask, so they do not have to contact support.

items.t: Questions taken from real support tickets and searches, not marketing points
Written in the customer's words
Short, direct answers; the first sentence answers the question
Links to longer help articles where needed
Grouped by topic with headings
Most asked questions first
Reviewed and dated; out-of-date answers removed
A search box over the questions on long pages
A list of all questions at the top that jumps to each answer
Each question has its own link that can be shared
Short lists may show all answers; long lists can fold into an accordion
Accordions are buttons with expanded and collapsed state
Find-in-page still works with folded answers (hidden="until-found" or all open)
Headings in order
"Still need help?" with a contact link at the end
"Was this helpful?" on each answer to find weak ones
FAQ structured data where it still applies (Google now shows it mainly for government and health sites)
Contrast and phone width meet WCAG

title: Features page
about: Shows what the product does, feature by feature, so visitors can judge whether it fits their need.

items.t: A headline that names the main outcome, not the technology
Features grouped by job or by user type, not a long flat list
Each feature: a short name, one benefit line and a real screenshot or clip
A jump list or tabs for long pages
Headings in order, so the page reads as an outline
Real product screens, not mock art, kept current with the product
A short customer quote or number next to the key features
Which plan includes each feature, linking to Pricing
Features still coming marked "Coming soon", never shown as available
Integrations listed with logos and a link to the full list
Links to docs or a help article for each feature
One main action (Start free, Book a demo) repeated after each few sections
A secondary path for people not ready (watch a tour, see pricing)
Videos have captions, no sound on start, and a pause control
Animated demos can be paused, and respect the reduced-motion setting
Screenshots have alt text describing what they show
Images sized and lazy-loaded so the page stays fast
Space reserved for images so the page does not jump while loading
A feature table for products with many plans or editions
Plain words for each feature, with a short explanation on demand

title: Footer
about: The bottom of every page: a safety net of links, contact and legal information.

items.t: Links grouped under short headings (Product, Company, Resources, Legal)
Contact: email, phone or a link to the contact page
Company name, registration and address where the law asks
Privacy policy, terms and cookie settings links
"Do not sell or share my personal information" where California law applies
Accessibility statement link
Copyright line with the current year
Social links with names, not only icons
Language and region switcher
Newsletter sign-up, short, with consent rules
Status page and help centre links
The same footer, in the same order, on every page
Help link in the same place on every page
Marked as the page's footer landmark (contentinfo)
Link groups are lists with headings
Link text says where it goes, no "click here"
Contrast meets 4.5 to 1, even on dark footers
Touch targets at least 24 pixels apart or in size
Groups stack or fold into sections on phones
Back to top link on long pages

title: Landing page
about: The page people arrive on from an ad, a link or a search; it has one job: get them to take one action.

items.t: A headline that says what the visitor gets, in their words
A sub-line that says how, or for whom
One main action button with a verb (Start free, Get the guide)
A product image or short clip that shows the real thing
The page matches the ad or link that brought the visitor (same promise, same words)
Three to five benefits, each a short heading, a line and a picture
Proof: customer logos, numbers or quotes, with permission
How it works in three steps
Answers to the main doubts (price, time, risk) in a short FAQ
The main action repeated after each big section
Few or no links that lead away from the action
Ask only what is needed; every extra field costs sign-ups
Labels above fields, the right keyboard and autofill
Errors in words next to the field
Marketing consent unticked by default where the law needs consent
Largest image or text shows in under 2.5 seconds
The page does not jump while loading
Responds to taps in under 200 milliseconds
Faster pages convert better (Vodafone, Rakuten and others measured it)
No fake countdowns, fake stock counts or hidden prices
Prices and terms in the page, not only in small print
Works at phone width with no sideways scroll
Contrast and text size meet WCAG
Buttons at least 24 by 24 pixels (44 recommended)
Video has captions, starts muted and can be paused
A page title and description written for search and sharing

title: Login page (website)
about: Lets returning people sign in quickly and safely, and recover when they cannot.

items.t: Email (or username) and password on one page, unless the site uses passkeys or single sign-on first
Real form with a form tag and a submit button, so Enter works and password managers save it
Visible labels, not placeholder-only
autocomplete set to username and current-password
Email field uses type email; no automatic capitals or spelling fixes
Pasting into the password field is allowed
Password managers and autofill are never blocked
Show password button with a clear name and state
Remember me (stay signed in) choice, with its length stated
Passkeys offered, with the browser's passkey autofill on the email field
Sign in with Google, Apple or work single sign-on where the audience uses them
Email magic link or one-time code as a choice for people without a password
The same ways shown on sign-up and sign-in, so people remember which they used
One error for a wrong email or password, never which one was wrong
Errors shown next to the field and focused, in words
Caps Lock warning on the password field
Limits on repeated wrong tries (slow down, then lock) with a message saying what to do
A robot check only after suspicious tries, and an accessible one
Two-step check after the password when the account has it
Signs in over HTTPS only; session cookie secure and httpOnly
New sign-ins from a new device announced by email
Forgot password link right beside the password field
A link to sign up for people without an account
Help or contact link for locked-out people
Back to the page they were on before signing in
No redirect to an outside address taken from the link
Focus starts on the first field, not stolen later
Contrast and target size meet WCAG
Works at phone width and with 200% text
Page title says "Sign in" with the site name
Use the same words everywhere: either "Sign in" or "Log in", not both

title: Newsletter sign-up
about: The small form where people give an email address to get news.

items.t: One email field with a clear label and type email
Says what they will get and how often
Consent wording clear, not hidden in terms
Separate from other consent (no bundled boxes)
Double opt-in by confirmation email where the law or deliverability needs it
A success message in the page
An unsubscribe link in every email, working with one click
The sender's name and postal address
Protection against bots without hard puzzles
Rate-limited by address
Link to the privacy notice

title: Press / Media page
about: Gives journalists what they need to write about the company quickly: news, facts, images and a contact.

items.t: A named press contact with email and phone, near the top
Expected reply time
Company fact sheet: founded, founders, headquarters, size, funding, what it does
Short and long company descriptions ready to copy
Leadership names, roles, bios and photos
Press releases listed newest first, each with a date and as HTML (not only PDF)
Coverage: links to articles about the company
Logos in several formats (SVG, PNG) on light and dark backgrounds
Product screenshots and photos at high resolution
One download for the whole kit, with its file size
Rules for using the logo and the brand name
Image credits and permission to use stated
Photos and logos have alt text
Downloads labelled with type and size
Contrast and headings meet WCAG
Reachable from the footer and About page

title: Pricing page (website)
about: Shows the plans and their prices so a visitor can pick one and start.

items.t: Two to four plans side by side, one marked as most popular
Each plan: name, who it is for, price, billing period and the main limits
Price in the visitor's currency, with tax shown or stated
Monthly and yearly switch, with the yearly saving as an amount, not only a percent
Yearly price also shown per month only if the full yearly charge is stated beside it
All mandatory fees inside the price shown
A free trial or free plan stated with what happens at the end
"Contact sales" only for the biggest plan; prices for the rest
A full feature table below the plan cards
Feature names in plain words with a short explanation on demand
Ticks also have words for screen readers
The table header stays visible while scrolling
FAQ: changing plans, cancelling, refunds, payment methods, discounts
How to cancel, and that it is as easy as signing up
Money-back promise, if any, with its terms
Customer logos or quotes near the plans
One button per plan with a clear verb (Start free trial, Buy Pro)
The chosen plan carries into sign-up and checkout
No pre-ticked add-ons, no fake discounts with made-up "was" prices
A struck-out old price only if it was the real price in the last 30 days (EU)
Plan cards stack on phones, the recommended one first
The monthly and yearly switch is a real control with a name and state
Contrast meets WCAG, including the highlighted plan

title: Privacy page
about: The privacy policy: what personal data is collected, why, who sees it, and what rights people have.

items.t: Who is responsible for the data: company name, address and contact
Contact for the data protection officer, if one is required
What data is collected, grouped by type (account, payment, usage, device)
Why each type is collected and the legal basis for it
Who data is shared with, by category, and whether it is sold
Transfers to other countries and how they are protected
How long each type is kept
People's rights: see, correct, delete, take away, object, withdraw consent
How to use those rights, with a direct link or form
The right to complain to the data authority
Whether any decisions are made automatically about people
Cookies and trackers explained, with a link to change choices
Children: minimum age and how children's data is handled
A "Do not sell or share my personal information" link where California law applies
A short summary at the top in plain words, the full text below
Written in clear, plain language; no hidden meaning
Headings and a contents list to jump to a part
Available in the languages the service is offered in
Effective date and a list of changes
People told by email when the policy changes in an important way
Linked from the footer of every page and from sign-up
Readable as plain HTML (not only a PDF)
Text contrast and size meet WCAG
A printable or downloadable version

title: Product page
about: The page for one product in a shop: pictures, price, options and the button to buy.

items.t: Several large images, including scale and in-use shots
Zoom on tap or hover
Images described for screen readers
Price with VAT and any fees shown before checkout
Options (size, colour) as visible choices, with unavailable ones marked
Stock and delivery date near the button
Specifications in a scannable list
Returns and warranty summary near the price
One clear Add to cart button that stays in reach on phones
Confirmation after adding, without taking the person away
Real reviews, with negative ones shown too
Product structured data (price, availability, rating)
Option choices work by keyboard and say which is selected

title: Search (website)
about: The search box and results on a website, so visitors find a page without browsing.

items.t: Shown as an open box, not hidden behind an icon, on sites with lots of content
At least 27 characters wide so queries are visible
A magnifier icon and a label or placeholder that says what can be searched
Has an accessible name and sits in a search landmark
Opens with a keyboard shortcut (/ or Ctrl+K) shown in the box
Enter submits; a clear button empties the box
Suggestions after 1 to 3 letters, at most about 8-10
Typed part plain, suggested part bold (or the other way, consistently)
Arrow keys move through suggestions, Escape closes them
Suggestion count announced to screen readers
Recent searches offered when the box is focused
The query stays in the box on the results page
Number of results shown
Each result: title, a short extract with the matched words highlighted, type and date
Typos forgiven, with "Did you mean ...?"
Filters by type, date or section for large sites
Sort by relevance by default
Pagination or "Load more" with the position kept on Back
Say so plainly, repeat the query, and offer fixes: spelling, fewer words, popular pages
A link to contact or browse
Results in under 1 second; show progress if slower
Page title includes the query ("Results for pricing")
Results page is not indexed by search engines

title: Security page
about: The public page that tells customers, buyers and researchers how the company protects their data and how to report a weakness.

items.t: One plain sentence that says what is protected and how, before any detail
Certifications held (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS) shown with the year and scope, never a badge for one not held
A link to request the full audit report (often under a confidentiality agreement)
A date showing when the page was last reviewed
A link to the live status page
Where data is stored (country or region) and which cloud providers are used
Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2 or newer) stated
Encryption at rest stated, with who holds the keys
How long data is kept and how it is deleted when an account closes
Backups: how often, where, and how often restores are tested
A list of sub-processors (third parties that handle customer data), with a way to be told of changes
Customer-side controls listed: two-step sign-in, single sign-on, roles, session timeout
Passkeys or other phishing-resistant sign-in offered or planned
Staff access to customer data: least privilege, logged, reviewed
How staff are vetted and trained in security
How the software is tested: code review, automatic scans, outside penetration tests and how often
Network protection named in plain terms (firewalls, DDoS protection) without giving attackers a map
Logging and monitoring of suspicious activity
Secrets (keys, passwords) kept in a managed vault, never in code
How customers are told about a breach, and how fast
A short incident-response outline: detect, contain, inform, review
Past incidents or a link to post-incident reports, if the company publishes them
A clear way to report a vulnerability: an email or form, what to include, and what happens next
A security.txt file at /.well-known/security.txt with contact, expiry and policy link
A safe-harbour statement: good-faith researchers will not be pursued
Response time promise (for example, first reply within 3 working days)
Bug bounty terms and rewards, if one exists, with what is out of scope
A PGP key or other way to send sensitive reports safely
Links to the privacy policy, data-processing agreement and terms
Laws the company follows named by region (GDPR, Saudi PDPL, CCPA)
Accessibility of the page itself: headings, contrast, readable without images
Written for a buyer, not an engineer: short sections, a jump list at the top
No vague claims like "bank-level security" or "military-grade"
A contact for security questions from buyers (security questionnaires)

title: Sign up page (website)
about: Creating an account on a website. The phone version (mobile/sign-up) has the full 65 items; this one adds what differs on a website.

items.t: What the person gets, in one line above the form
Let people try or buy without an account where possible
Price and trial terms visible before the form if sign-up starts a trial
Sign up with Google, Apple, Microsoft or work single sign-on, matched to the audience
Passkey offered at or right after sign-up, with a fallback
Email and password as the always-there choice
Ask only what is needed now; everything else later
One name field ("Full name"), not first and last, for international names
Visible labels; placeholders only as examples
autocomplete set: name, email, new-password
Optional fields marked "(optional)"; required ones not starred
Email typo hint ("Did you mean gmail.com?")
At least 8 characters (15 if it is the only factor), up to at least 64, any characters
No rules like "one capital, one symbol"; check against known leaked passwords instead

Collapse a column
Swimlanes (rows) by person, priority or project
Title, assignee photo, due date, labels and a small set of icons (comments, files)

Quick "Only my cards" filter

Moving by keyboard announced ("Card moved to Doing, position 2")

Focus visible on cards

items.t: Shortcuts for the most frequent actions only

Destructive shortcuts can be undone

title: List View

items.t: Each row: the name first, then two or three key facts

Filter and search above the list
Active filters shown with remove

Drag to reorder where order matters, with a keyboard way too
Swipe actions on touch screens, with a visible alternative
Pagination or load more, with the total
Back keeps the scroll position
Skeleton rows while loading
Empty and no-results states
A real list (or table if there are columns)
Row links read well alone
Touch targets at least 24 by 24 pixels
Works at phone width

items.t: Email or username, then password or passkey

"Keep me signed in" for trusted devices

Forgot password link next to the password field
Link to sign up and to help
Errors next to fields and in a summary, focus moved there

title: Maintenance
about: What people see when the app is down for planned work or an outage, and the warnings before it.

items.t: Warned ahead in the app and by email: date, start time with time zone, how long, what stops working
Planned at a quiet time for most users
A banner a day before and an hour before, which can be closed
Listed on the status page

When it should be back, with time zone

Text readable, contrast meets WCAG, no animation-only message
Auto reload does not move focus or surprise screen readers
In the app's languages

title: Multi-step form
about: A long form split into steps (a wizard), so people answer a few questions at a time.

items.t: Split only when the form is long or later questions depend on earlier answers
One topic per step; one question per page for hard or unfamiliar questions
Steps named, with "Step 2 of 5" and a progress indicator

Continue and Back buttons in the same places on every step
Browser Back works and keeps answers
Answers saved as people go; leaving and coming back continues
Save and come back later, for long forms

Errors checked when leaving a field or on Continue, never while typing the first time
Error summary at the top of the step, linking to each field
Error message next to each field in words

Labels, autofill and the right keyboard on every field

Works at phone width

title: Notification Settings
about: Where people choose what they are told about, and how (email, in-app, push, text).

items.t: Grouped by topic (mentions, comments, billing, security, product news)
A grid: topics down the side, channels across the top (email, push, in-app)
Each row says in plain words what triggers it
Defaults set to what most people want, never to everything
Switches or checkboxes with clear names that include the topic and channel
Changes saved at once, with a short "Saved" message announced to screen readers

Quiet hours with the time zone

One-click unsubscribe in every marketing email, honoured quickly

Links in each email to change the setting for that topic

title: Notifications (web app)
about: The in-app list (often a bell) of things that happened which the person may need to act on.

items.t: An icon button with a name and the unread count ("Notifications, 3 unread")
Count capped (9+) and shown as a badge
New notifications announced politely, not interrupting
Newest first, grouped by today, this week, older
Each item: who, what, on which item, and when (relative time, exact on hover)
Unread items marked by more than colour (a dot plus bold)
Clicking opens the item and marks it read
Mark one or all as read
Quick actions inline (approve, reply) for common jobs
Filters: all, mentions, assigned to me
Link to notification settings
Similar notifications combined ("Sara and 4 others commented")
Only things the person cares about; let them mute a thread
Old notifications cleared after a stated time
Empty state: "You're all caught up"
Loading and error states
The panel is a dialog or popover with focus moved in and Escape to close
List items reachable by keyboard
Works at phone width (full-screen panel)

title: Onboarding (web app)
about: The first minutes in the app after sign-up, getting the person to their first real success.

items.t: Lead to the first useful result fast ("aha moment"), not a tour of every feature
Ask a few setup questions only if the answers change what they see
Each question skippable, with a sensible default
A progress indicator for multi-step setup
A checklist of first tasks that ticks itself as they are done
Hints at the moment a feature is first used, not all at once
Tours short (3 to 5 steps), skippable, and restartable from help
Templates or sample data to start from, easy to delete
Empty states that teach (see the Empty State note)
Invite teammates offered after the person has done something useful
Import from other tools (CSV, competitors) offered early
No forced long tutorials or video before use
Permissions (notifications, location) asked only when needed, with why
Marketing consent separate from setup
Onboarding state saved, so leaving and coming back continues where they were
Tour popovers reachable by keyboard, with focus moved in and back out
Tour highlights do not hide the focused element
Animations respect reduced motion

title: Pricing (inside the app)
about: The plans page shown to signed-in users, with their current plan and what changing would cost.

items.t: Current plan marked clearly
2 to 4 plans side by side, one suggested
Price per month and per year, with the yearly saving
Prices include or exclude VAT, stated clearly
Per-seat prices show the total for the team's size
Currency of the account (SAR for Saudi customers)
The features that differ, not a wall of ticks
Feature names with short explanations on hover or tap
Limits stated in numbers (projects, storage, members)
The person's own usage shown next to each plan's limit
Upgrade shows prorated charge today and the next bill
Downgrade shows what will be lost or locked, and when it takes effect
Owners change plans; members can request
Contact sales for large plans, without hiding the price of smaller ones
No fake countdowns or "only 2 left"
Trial terms and auto-renewal stated before payment
Cancellation easy to find from here
Comparison table with headers; ticks have text for screen readers
Works at phone width (plans stack, table scrolls)
Monthly/yearly switch is a real switch or radio group

title: Public Profile
about: The page other people see about a user: who they are and what they have made or shared.

items.t: Name, photo, short bio and role
What the person has made or shared (posts, projects, reviews)
Join date and simple activity numbers
Links to their other profiles, marked as external
Verified badges explained on hover or tap
Follow, message or contact, if the product has them
Share profile link
Report or block the person, easy to find
The owner sees what is public, with a "View as visitor" preview
Choose what is public field by field; private by default for sensitive data
No email, phone or exact location shown unless the owner chose it
Hide profile from search engines option

A readable address (/@name) that does not change silently
Person structured data where useful
Page title with the person's name

Headings for sections; contrast and phone width meet WCAG

title: Report View
about: One finished report: a set of numbers, charts and tables about a period or a subject, for reading and sharing.

items.t: Report title, the period covered and who made it
When the data was taken, and the time zone
Filters applied shown at the top
Summary of the key findings first, in words
Numbers with comparison to a previous period or a target
Charts with titles that state the point ("Sales rose 12% in March")
Tables with totals and subtotals
Notes and definitions for each number
Export to PDF and spreadsheet
Share link with permissions (who can see)
Schedule by email (weekly, monthly)
Print layout that fits pages and repeats table headers

Personal data hidden or grouped unless needed
Headings in order so the report reads as an outline
Charts have a text summary or data table
Exported PDF tagged and readable by screen readers
Colour not the only way to show good or bad

title: Reporting
about: The tool for building, saving, scheduling and sharing reports (the Report View note covers reading one).

items.t: Start from templates for common questions
Choose data, measures (sum, count, average) and grouping in plain words
Preview updates as choices change
Filters and date range with presets

items.t: A few clear default roles (owner, admin, member, viewer)

Sort by name or last active

Long text wraps or truncates with full text on hover and focus
Totals row marked as such

title: Tabs
about: A row of labels that switch between views of related content in the same place.

items.t: Switching between related views of the same thing (Overview, Activity, Settings)
Not for steps in order (use a stepper) or for main navigation of the app (use a nav bar)
Not when people need to compare content across tabs
Short labels, one or two words, in a single row
Selected tab clearly marked by more than colour (underline, weight)
Tabs look connected to their content
Icons optional; never icons alone without names
Too many to fit: scroll sideways with visible arrows, or a "More" menu
Switching is instant; content keeps its state when coming back
Selected tab kept in the address when tabs are big views
Swipe between tabs on phones, with taps too
Counts or badges on tabs when useful ("Comments 3")
Tab list, tab and tab panel roles; each tab controls its panel
Arrow keys move between tabs; Tab goes into the panel
Home and End jump to first and last
Selected tab marked aria-selected
Panel labelled by its tab
Arrows flip for right-to-left
Targets large enough to tap

title: Tag and chip
about: Small labels for status or category, and small buttons for filters and choices.

items.t: Status tags (read only) kept apart from chips you can press
Filter chips toggle and show they are on
Input chips (like email addresses) have a remove button
Short, one or two words
Meaning not given by colour alone
Pressable chips are buttons with a pressed state
Remove buttons named ("Remove Riyadh")
Text contrast meets 4.5:1
Tap targets at least 24 by 24 pixels

title: Text area
about: The box for writing longer text, like comments or descriptions.

items.t: A visible label and optional help text
Height fits the expected answer; grows as you type where possible
A character count when there is a limit, updated politely to screen readers
Going over the limit allowed while typing, then shown as an error
Spell check on
Direction follows the text (dir=auto) for mixed Arabic and English
Drafts saved for long text
Errors linked to the field
Resizable and not clipped when text is enlarged

title: Toast
about: A short message that appears for a few seconds to confirm an action (also called a snackbar), then goes away.

items.t: Low-importance confirmations ("Saved", "Message sent")
An undo right after an action ("Deleted. Undo")
Not for errors that need action or anything the person must read
Not for the result of a form submit that fails (show errors in the form)
One short line; at most one action
The action is never the only way to do it (undo is also in a menu)
Fixed place (bottom centre or bottom start) across the product
Above the tab bar on phones
Contrast meets WCAG
One at a time; later ones wait
Stays long enough to read: about 4 to 10 seconds, longer with an action
Pauses on hover and focus
Can be closed
With reduced motion, appears without sliding
Announced by screen readers with a status region (polite)
Does not take focus from what the person was doing
Action reachable by keyboard (a shortcut to jump to it helps)
Does not cover focused content or buttons

title: Toggle
about: A switch that turns one setting on or off and takes effect at once.

items.t: A setting that applies immediately (Notifications on)
Not inside a form with a Save button (use a checkbox)
Not for choosing between two different things (use radios or a segmented control)
Track and thumb; on and off clearly different by position and fill, not only colour
An optional check icon inside the thumb when on
Label on the start side says what is switched, not the state ("Email alerts")
Track border and thumb 3:1 contrast in both states
Touch area at least 24 px, ideally 44 to 48
Changes apply at once, with a short "Saved" message if it is saved to a server
If saving fails, the toggle goes back and an error says why
If the change is slow, a busy state
Labels never change meaning with the state ("On" text can confuse)
Disabled toggles explain why
role switch with aria-checked, or a native checkbox styled as a switch
Space toggles; Enter may too
Label linked to the switch
Focus ring visible
Thumb moves to the other side in right-to-left
Animation respects reduced motion

title: Tokens
about: Named design values (colours, sizes, spacing, radius, motion) that design and code share as one source.

items.t: Primitive tokens: raw values named by what they are (blue-600, space-4)
Role (semantic) tokens: named by job (color-primary, space-gap-md), pointing to primitives
Component tokens: named per component (button-bg), pointing to roles
Components use role or component tokens, never primitives
Stored in the W3C design tokens format (JSON with $value and $type)
Each token has a type (color, dimension, fontFamily, duration, shadow)
References use {group.token} so one change flows everywhere
A description on each role token saying when to use it
Names follow one pattern (category-role-variant-state)
No names that describe looks for role tokens ("blue-button")
Avoid names that clash with tool names (Tailwind sizes)
Light, dark and high-contrast as sets of role values over the same primitives
Brands or products as further sets
Density and size modes (compact, comfortable)
One source file builds CSS variables, Tailwind config, iOS and Android values
The design tool reads the same file
Changes reviewed and versioned like code (semver)
A check fails the build when a component uses a raw value
Colour, typography, spacing, size, radius, border, shadow, opacity, motion duration and easing, z-index
Contrast pairs of colour tokens tested automatically
Every token shown with its value, a preview and where it is used
Deprecated tokens marked with what replaces them

title: Tooltip
about: A small label that appears near an element on hover or keyboard focus, to name it or add a short hint.

items.t: Naming icon-only buttons, and short hints that are nice to have
Never for information people need to finish a task (put it on the page)
Never for interactive content like links or buttons (use a popover)
Not on touch screens alone: they have no hover
A few words; one sentence at most
No repetition of the visible label
Close to the element, not covering it or what it relates to
Moves to stay on screen
Contrast meets WCAG
An arrow pointing at the element is optional
Appears after a short delay (about 300 to 500 ms) on hover, at once on focus
Stays while the pointer is over the tooltip itself
Closes with Escape without moving focus
Closes when focus or pointer leaves
role tooltip, linked from the element with aria-describedby (hint) or used as its name (aria-labelledby)
Shows on keyboard focus, not only on hover
The element still has a name without the tooltip for screen readers
Disabled buttons: put the tooltip on a wrapper that can take focus, or explain on the page

title: Typography
about: The text styles of a design system: fonts, sizes, weights, line heights and how they are used.

items.t: A small set of named roles (display, heading, title, body, label, caption) instead of free sizes
Sizes from a scale with a steady ratio
Body text at least 16 px on the web
Each role sets font, size, weight, line height and letter spacing together
Styles stored as tokens
Line length about 45 to 80 characters
Line height about 1.4 to 1.6 for body text, tighter for headings
Text still works when people increase spacing (line, letter, word, paragraph)
Left-aligned (start-aligned) body text, not justified
Few weights; bold for real emphasis only
Sizes in rem so they follow the browser's text size
Text can grow to 200% without cut-off or overlap
On iOS and Android, follow the system text size (Dynamic Type, font scale)
Body text contrast at least 4.5:1, large text 3:1
APCA checked for thin or small fonts
No light grey text for important information
Fonts cover every language used (Arabic and Latin), matched in size and weight
Arabic needs more line height and should not be letter-spaced
Numbers in tables use tabular figures
Fallback fonts listed; fonts load without hiding text (font-display swap)
Visual style separate from heading level: a heading role can be any size
Headings in order on each page
No text in images

title: Account (mobile)
about: The account area of a phone app: personal details, sign-in, security, data and deleting the account.

items.t: Name, email, phone, each editable with its own screen
Changing email or phone confirmed by a code to the new one
Current password or Face ID asked before sensitive changes
Change password; add a passkey
Two-step check on and off, with backup codes
Signed-in devices with "Sign out" each and "Sign out everywhere"
Linked accounts (Apple, Google) with unlink, if another way in remains
Download my data
Privacy choices (ads, tracking)
Account deletion possible inside the app if the app lets people create accounts
A web link to delete the account too, for Google Play
Say what is deleted, what is kept by law and how long it takes
Store subscriptions: remind to cancel in the store, with a link
Confirm with password or typed word; never a one-tap delete
Clear Sign out at the bottom, with a confirmation
Rows named with their value
Large text supported; rows at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Action Sheet
about: A list of actions that slides up from the bottom of the phone screen, about the thing just tapped.

items.t: Choices about one item (Share, Edit, Delete) or confirming a destructive action
Android uses a bottom sheet or a menu for the same job
Not for long content or forms (use a full sheet or new screen)
Not for a simple yes/no that needs explanation (use an alert)
Optional title and message saying what the actions are about
Short action names, verbs first
Destructive action styled red and placed at the top on iOS
A Cancel button at the bottom, separate from the rest
Few actions; long lists scroll
Tap outside or swipe down closes it
Android back closes it
On iPad and large screens it shows as a popover next to what was tapped
Destructive actions can be undone, or confirmed
Grabber handle on draggable sheets
Dimmed background behind
Rows at least 44 pt / 48 dp tall
Focus moves into the sheet and returns after
Screen readers announce it as a menu or dialog with a title
Large text grows the rows instead of cutting text

title: Activity Feed (mobile)
about: A scrolling list of updates in a phone app: posts, events, or what people and things did.

items.t: Each: who, what, when, with photo or icon and a short preview
Times as "5 min ago" with the full date on tap or for screen readers
Similar events grouped ("Sara and 4 others...")
Tap opens the full item
Newest first; "New posts" pill at the top instead of jumping the list
Pull to refresh
Endless scroll with a loading row; position kept when coming back
Skeleton rows on first load
Images loaded small first, videos play muted only when visible, if at all
Filters (all, mentions, following) as tabs or chips
Hide, mute, or report an item from its menu
Chronological option where the order is ranked
No tricks to keep scrolling (fake new items, autoplay chains)
"You're all caught up" at the end of new items
Cached items shown with a notice
Each item a single readable unit with actions as custom actions
Autoplay can be turned off; reduced motion respected
Large text supported; targets at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: App update
about: Getting people onto a new version, and forcing it only when really needed.

items.t: Flexible in-app update prompts for normal releases
Forced updates only for security or broken old versions
The prompt says what is new or why it matters
The server knows the minimum supported version and answers old versions clearly
APIs keep working for older app versions for a set time
What's new shown once, briefly, skippable
Release notes in the store listing

title: Billing (mobile)
about: Seeing and managing subscriptions and payments inside a phone app.

items.t: Digital subscriptions bought through Apple or Google in-app purchase (with regional exceptions)
Current plan, price, renewal date and the store it was bought from
"Manage subscription" opens the store's own subscription page
Restore purchases button for people on a new phone
Upgrades and downgrades through the store, with the price change shown
Free trial end date and the first charge shown clearly
If the plan was bought on the web, say so and where to manage it
Rules on linking to the website for payment differ by country and store; follow the current guideline
Saved payment methods with brand and last 4 digits
Order and payment history with receipts
VAT invoices for Saudi customers
Cancel as easy as subscribing; the path is clear
What happens after cancelling: access until the period ends
Billing problem (card failed at the store): banner with a link to fix it in the store
Grace period respected: access continues while the store retries
Prices read clearly with currency by screen readers
Large text and buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Camera
about: Taking photos, videos or scanning (documents, QR codes) inside a phone app.

items.t: Ask for camera access only when the person taps to use it
A clear purpose string ("To scan your receipt")
If refused: explain and offer a button to settings, plus another way (pick from photos, type the code)
Use the system photo picker to choose photos without asking for full library access
Large shutter button reachable by thumb
Flash, switch camera and close buttons with names
Guides for scanning (a frame for documents, a square for QR)
Auto-capture when a document or code is steady, with manual capture too
Feedback on success (sound or haptic and a visual mark)
Preview with Retake and Use photo
Crop, rotate and simple fixes
Upload with progress; works again if the connection drops
Location in photos removed unless needed and stated
Photos stored only where the person expects; say where
Camera stops when leaving the screen; system indicator shows when it is on
VoiceOver and TalkBack users get spoken hints ("Document found, hold still")
Alternatives for people who cannot use the camera (upload, type)
Works in both orientations where it makes sense

title: Cart (mobile)
about: The shopping cart screen of a phone app, before checkout.

items.t: Each item: photo, name, options (size, colour), price and quantity
Quantity with minus and plus buttons; removing at zero asks or offers undo
Remove and Save for later
Out of stock or price changed items marked clearly at the top
Tap item opens its product screen
Subtotal, delivery, discounts, VAT and total, with delivery estimate
Free delivery threshold progress ("Add 30 SAR for free delivery")
Promo code field folded, not a big empty box
Checkout button sticky at the bottom with the total
Apple Pay or Google Pay express button where available
Continue shopping link
Cart kept across sessions and devices when signed in
Cart badge on the tab or icon with the count
Empty cart: friendly message and suggestions
Adding to cart confirms with a small message, haptic and badge change, without leaving the product
Changes to quantity update the total at once
Quantity buttons named ("Increase quantity of Blue shirt")
Total changes announced
Large text supported; buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Chat (mobile)
about: Messaging inside a phone app: the list of conversations and one conversation with its message box.

items.t: Newest first: photo, name, last message, time, unread count
Search across conversations
Swipe for archive, mute, delete, with a menu too
Pinned conversations at the top
Messages grouped by sender and day; own messages on one side
Status per message: sending, sent, delivered, read (with icons and words for screen readers)
Failed message marked with Retry
Typing indicator for the other person
Opens at the last unread message; "jump to latest" button
Long press for reply, copy, react, forward, delete
Grows with text; send button only active with content
Keyboard never covers the box or the last message
Attach photos, files, voice notes, location
Draft kept when leaving the conversation
Right-to-left and mixed Arabic and English text shown in the right direction per message
Photos load as small previews first; tap opens full screen with zoom
Voice notes with length and a play bar
Upload progress and cancel
Block and report from the conversation
End-to-end encryption where private messages are expected; say so
Notifications can hide message text on the lock screen
New messages announced politely
Each message read with sender and time
Large text supported; targets at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Checkout (mobile)
about: Paying for physical goods or services in a phone app, from cart to confirmation.

items.t: As few screens as possible; guest checkout allowed
Progress shown for multi-step checkout
Order summary can be expanded on each step, with the total always visible
Sticky bottom bar with the total and the main button
Address from saved addresses or autofill; map pin for places without clear addresses
Delivery options with price and date
Phone number with country code picker, numeric keyboard
Apple Pay and Google Pay first where available
Local methods (mada, STC Pay, cash on delivery) where they suit
Card fields from a certified provider, card scan with the camera
Strong customer authentication (3-D Secure) opened inside the app
Physical goods and services may use any payment provider
Digital goods and subscriptions must use in-app purchase (with regional exceptions)
All fees, delivery and tax shown before the final button
Promo code field quiet, not a big empty box
Button names the amount ("Pay 245 SAR")
Busy state; no double charge
Declined payment explained, details kept
Confirmation screen with order number and tracking
Receipt and VAT invoice by email
Offer push alerts for delivery here (see Push Opt-in)
Large text, VoiceOver and TalkBack work on every step
Buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp
Keyboard never hides the active field or the button

title: Dashboard (mobile)
about: The overview screen in a phone app with key numbers, status and things to act on.

items.t: Top 2 to 4 numbers that matter most, large
Change from the last period with arrow and word, not only colour
Things needing action at the top (due, overdue, waiting)
Every card taps through to its detail
One column of cards; a horizontal swipe row only for secondary items
Simple charts sized for a phone (sparklines, small bars)
Period choice (today, week, month) at the top
Last updated time; pull to refresh
Cached data shown at once, then refreshed
Cards load on their own with skeletons
Works offline with cached numbers marked as old
Choose and reorder cards
Home screen widgets for the key number (iOS and Android)
Charts have text summaries for screen readers
Cards are headings or buttons with clear names
Large text reflows cards instead of cutting numbers
Targets at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Deep links
about: Links that open a specific screen in the app.

items.t: Verified app links on Android and universal links on iPhone
The same address works on the web when the app is not installed
Opens the exact screen, with a back path that makes sense
Sign-in required? Sign in, then continue to the linked screen
Missing or deleted content: a clear message, not a crash
Every linked screen checks permission
Parameters validated like any input
Each link tested installed, not installed and signed out

title: Empty state (mobile)
about: What a phone screen shows when there is nothing in it yet.

items.t: Says why it is empty and what to do
One main action button
A small picture only if it helps, not big blocks of art
First use, no results, cleared and error states each handled
Fits small screens and large text without scrolling far
Pictures marked as decorative or described

title: Feedback (mobile)
about: Asking for ratings, reviews, bug reports and ideas inside a phone app.

items.t: Use the system review prompt (SKStoreReviewController / In-App Review API)
Ask after a success moment, never on first launch or during a task
The system limits how often it shows (3 times a year on iOS); do not build your own star prompt that sends only happy users to the store
No rewards for ratings
"Send feedback" in Settings and Help
Short form: what happened, optional screenshot, optional email
Screenshot shake or attach, with the chance to blur private parts
Device, app version and system version attached automatically, with notice
Thank-you and what happens next
One question at a time, at most 2 or 3
Easy to close; not shown again soon after
Answers come back in the app or by email; the person can follow their report
Ratings with buttons, not only swipes
Form fields named; large text supported
Buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Gesture navigation
about: Moving around an app with swipes and other gestures, alongside the system's own gestures.

items.t: Do not take over the system's edge swipes (home, back, notifications)
Android back gesture: use the predictive back so people see where they go
iOS swipe from the left edge goes back in navigation stacks; keep it working
Content drawn edge to edge, with controls kept away from gesture areas
Use standard gestures with their usual meaning (tap, swipe, pinch, long press, pull to refresh)
Swipe actions on list rows (archive, delete) shown with colour, icon and text
Every gesture has a visible alternative (button or menu)
Gestures that need two fingers or a path have a single-tap way too
Destructive swipes can be undone
Hint at hidden gestures (a peek of the swipe action, a handle on sheets)
No reliance on gestures nobody can discover
Movement follows the finger and can be cancelled mid-way
Light haptics confirm a completed gesture, where supported
Reduced motion respected for the animations
Works with VoiceOver and TalkBack (custom actions for swipe actions)
Accidental activation avoided (actions on release, not on touch down)
Shake or tilt never the only way to do something

title: Home screen widgets
about: Small views of the app on the home screen.

items.t: One clear job per widget with glanceable information
Sizes offered that fit the content
Tapping opens the matching screen
Updates on a sensible schedule, not constantly
Placeholder content while loading
No private data shown without the person choosing it
Follows system light and dark mode
Text scales with system settings

title: In-App Browser
about: Opening web pages inside a phone app instead of switching to the phone's browser.

items.t: Use the system's in-app browser (SFSafariViewController on iOS, Custom Tabs on Android), not a home-made web view, for outside sites
The system kind shares the person's browser sign-ins and autofill, and the app cannot read what they type
Sign-in with an outside provider (OAuth) uses the system sign-in sheet (ASWebAuthenticationSession) or Custom Tabs, never a web view
Done or close button, address (domain) shown, share, and "Open in browser"
Loading bar
Back and forward when the page has history
The domain is visible so people know where they are
No injected scripts or tracking in pages that are not the app's own
Only https
Short visits (an article, help page, terms) that should return to the app
Links to other apps (maps, phone, mail) open those apps
App's own content better built as real screens than web pages
Close button named and at least 44 pt / 48 dp
Text size follows the system where the page allows

title: In-App Notifications
about: Messages shown inside the phone app while it is open: a notifications list, banners at the top, and badges.

items.t: A notifications screen reached from a bell or a tab, newest first
Each item: who, what, when, with a photo or icon
Unread marked by a dot and bold, not only colour
Tap opens the right screen and marks it read
Swipe to delete or mark read, with buttons too
Mark all as read
Empty state: "You're all caught up"

sections.name: Banners while the app is open

items.t: A short banner at the top for important new things, which goes away by itself
Does not cover the main action or the keyboard
Tap opens it; swipe up dismisses
Not shown for the conversation the person is already in
Similar items combined ("Sara and 3 others liked...")
Settings to choose topics, reachable from the list
App icon badge count matches the unread count
New banners announced by VoiceOver and TalkBack without moving focus
Banners stay long enough to read, or can be found again in the list
Items readable with large text
Targets at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Invite (mobile)
about: Inviting people into a shared space in a phone app (a team, household, group or document), not for a reward.

items.t: Share a link through the system share sheet
Type an email or phone number
Pick from contacts only after the person chooses it, with a reason
QR code to scan in person
Choose what the invited person can do (view, edit, admin), with one-line explanations
Default is the safest useful role
Expiry and "reset link" to stop an old link working
Approval by an admin optional for link joins
List of sent invites with state (waiting, accepted), resend and cancel
Accepted invites move to the members list
Link opens the app (or the store, then the right screen after install)
Says who invited them and to what, before they join
Accept or decline
No messages sent to contacts without the person's action
Contacts not uploaded or kept without consent
Role choices as a list with radio buttons and names
Large text supported; buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Login (mobile)
about: Signing in to a phone app with password, passkey, code, biometrics or another account.

items.t: Passkeys offered where supported
Sign in with Apple on iOS if other social sign-ins are offered
Google sign-in through the system Credential Manager on Android
Phone number with SMS code, with the code autofilled from the message
Email or phone field with the right keyboard and autofill type
Password field works with password managers (no blocked paste)
Show password button
Login button stays usable; errors after submit
Stay signed in by default on a personal phone
Face ID or fingerprint to unlock the app later, as an option
Tokens kept in the Keychain or Keystore, not plain storage
One general message for wrong email or password
Forgot password link near the field
Too many tries: wait time shown, not a dead end
Offline: say so, keep what was typed
Two-step check where risk is high
New device sign-in alert by email
Fields have visible names, not placeholders only
Large text supported; keyboard never covers the button
Buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Map View
about: A map inside a phone app showing places, routes or the person's location, often with a list beside it.

items.t: Ask only when the map needs the person's location, with a clear reason
Ask for "while using the app" first; background location only when truly needed
Approximate location accepted where exact is not needed
If refused: the map still works with search or a typed address
Standard gestures: drag, pinch, double tap to zoom, two-finger rotate
Zoom buttons or another way for people who cannot pinch
"My location" button that centres the map
Pins clear and grouped (clustered) when crowded
Selected pin highlighted, with a card showing details
Map style follows dark mode
Toggle or bottom sheet to switch between map and list
Moving the map offers "Search this area" instead of reloading on every move
List order matches what is visible on the map
Distance and time shown in local units
Open in the phone's maps app for directions
Arabic place names and right-to-left labels where relevant
Map tiles cached; usage of map services counted against limits
Few markers drawn at once
A list view with the same places for screen readers
Pins have names; selected place announced
Controls at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Offline
about: What an app does with no connection or a weak one.

items.t: Recent data shown from the device when offline
Changes saved on the device and sent when back online
Conflicts resolved by a clear rule
A quiet banner when offline, not an error on every screen
Actions that need a connection say so
Items waiting to send are marked
Retries with growing waits when the connection returns
No data lost when the app closes while offline
Service worker caches the shell and key data

title: Onboarding (mobile)
about: The first screens of a phone app after install, before the person starts using it.

items.t: Get people into the app fast; onboarding as short as possible
Skip button on every intro slide
Intro slides only if the app is new in kind; 3 at most
Teach in context (hints when a feature is first used) rather than up front
Let people look around before signing up where the app allows
Sign up later, when needed (saving, buying)
Sign in with Apple offered if other social sign-ins are offered on iOS
A few questions only if the answers shape the experience (interests, goals)
Each skippable with sensible defaults
Progress shown
Ask one at a time, at the moment it is needed, with a pre-permission screen
App works if the person says no
App Tracking Transparency prompt only if the app tracks across apps
Marketing and tracking consent separate, never pre-ticked
Age checks for apps with age limits
Slides work with VoiceOver and TalkBack (swipe and buttons)
Animations respect reduced motion
Text readable at large sizes; buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Onboarding Checklist
about: A short list of first tasks in a new account (add photo, invite a friend, turn on alerts) that ticks off as they are done.

items.t: 3 to 6 tasks that lead to real value, most important first
Each task: short name, why it helps, and a button that goes straight to it
One task can already be done to start ("Account created")
Time to do each task, if more than a minute
"2 of 5 done" with a bar
Tasks tick themselves when done anywhere in the app
A small reward or message at the end, then the checklist goes away
On the home screen as a card, can be collapsed
Can be hidden or skipped; reachable again from settings or help
Never blocks using the app
Notifications, contacts or location tasks open a pre-permission screen first
Saying no does not leave the checklist stuck: the task can be skipped
Progress announced in words
Done shown by tick and word, not only colour
Rows at least 44 pt / 48 dp; large text supported

title: Paywall
about: The screen that asks people to subscribe or buy to unlock content or features in a phone app.

items.t: Digital content and features sold through Apple and Google in-app purchase (with regional exceptions)
The price, the billing period and what is included shown clearly near the buy button
Price per period is the most prominent price; any per-week or per-month breakdown is secondary
Free trial: length, what it turns into, and when the first charge happens
Links to terms of use and privacy policy
Restore purchases button
What the person gets, in 3 to 5 short benefits
Plans side by side (monthly, yearly) with the saving
Social proof only if true and current
The screen is honest about what stays free
A visible way to close the paywall; no hidden or delayed close button
Not shown on first launch before the app has shown value, unless the app is paid-only
No fake timers or "only today" prices that are not true
Not shown repeatedly after being closed
Access unlocked at once, with a thank-you
Receipt from the store
How to manage or cancel shown in settings
Prices read clearly by screen readers with the currency
Close button has a name and is at least 44 pt / 48 dp
Large text supported without hiding the price or buttons

title: Permission prompts
about: Asking for camera, location, contacts or notifications at the right time.

items.t: Ask when the person uses the feature that needs it, not at launch
Explain why first, in the app, before the system prompt
The system prompt text (purpose string) is specific
Ask for the least access (approximate location, chosen photos)
The app still works without it
A way to turn it on later, with a link to settings
No repeated nagging
Android 13 and later need the notification permission
App Tracking Transparency before tracking on iPhone

title: Profile (mobile)
about: A person's profile screen in a phone app: their own (editable) and other people's (viewed).

items.t: Photo, name, short bio and key counts (posts, followers)
Verified marks explained on tap
Main action clear: Edit profile on your own, Follow or Message on others
Tabs for the person's content (posts, saved, likes), each with an empty state
Pull to refresh
Long bios cut with "more"
Edit opens a form screen with Save and Cancel
Change photo: take, choose from photos (system picker) or remove
Crop to the shape shown
Username rules shown before saving; checked as typed
What is public is marked; preview "as others see it"
More menu with Share, Block, Report
Blocking explained (what they will and will not see)
Private accounts show a clear locked state
Only needed details public by default
Contact details hidden unless chosen
Photo has the person's name as its description
Counts read with their meaning ("120 followers")

title: Pull to refresh
about: Pulling a list down to load the newest items.

items.t: On lists that show changing content, in time order
Not the only way to refresh; a button or automatic refresh as well
The system control, so it feels native
Indicator shows while loading and disappears when done
New items appear without jumping the person's place
A failed refresh says so and keeps the old content
Screen readers have a refresh action

title: Push Notification Opt-in
about: Asking a phone user for permission to send push notifications, and handling yes, no and later.

items.t: Ask when the person has a reason to want alerts (after ordering: "Get delivery updates?"), not at first launch
A pre-permission screen in the app's own words first, then the system prompt only if they say yes
The system prompt on iOS can be shown only once; a "Not now" on the pre-screen keeps that chance
Android 13 and later need the runtime permission too
Says what kinds of alerts and how often ("Only when your order moves")
One clear yes button and an equal "Not now"
An example of a notification
Yes: confirm and offer choices of topics in settings
No: the app works fully without it
Later: ask again only at a new, relevant moment, not on every launch
If turned off in system settings, show how to turn it back on, with a button to the settings page
Provisional authorization: quiet notifications delivered without asking, so the person can decide later
Time-sensitive and critical alerts only for real needs
Push not used for ads unless the person opted in to marketing
Marketing consent separate from service alerts
Notification channels on Android so people can mute kinds separately
Pre-screen readable with large text and screen readers
Buttons at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Referral (mobile)
about: Inviting others with a personal link or code, where both sides may get a reward.

items.t: What both sides get, in one line ("You both get 25 SAR")

Reward shown in the person's currency
Personal link and code, with Copy (and a confirmation)
System share sheet so people choose the app themselves
Ready message they can edit; no messages sent without their action
Contacts access only if they choose "pick from contacts", with a reason
List of invited people and the state of each (joined, rewarded)
Total earned and where to use it
Rewards in digital credits follow store payment rules
No rewards for app reviews or ratings
Fraud checks without blocking real users
Referred person told they came through a referral
Code readable by screen readers letter by letter
Copy and share buttons named; at least 44 pt / 48 dp

title: Search (mobile)

items.t: Search in a tab, or a search field at the top of the main list

Recent searches, with remove and clear all
Popular or suggested searches
Categories to browse
Suggestions after a character or two

Search key on the keyboard
Clear button and Cancel (iOS) or back arrow (Android)
Voice search where it helps

Matched words highlighted with weight, not only colour
Filters in a sheet or chips above results, with counts
Sort choice
Infinite scroll keeps position when coming back
Say so, show the words, suggest spelling fixes and other searches
Field has a name ("Search products")
Number of results announced
